title: Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization Analysis for Type 1 Diabetes Biomarkers
author: Songbai Liu
materials: Visualize top enriched pathways using enrichplot.
Identify overlapping miRNAs from both databases.
Map chromosomal locations of final biomarkers using RCircos.
Retrieve subcellular localization from GeneCards database (https://www.genecards.org/).
Perform molecular docking using PyRx software (v0.8.0): Binding energy threshold: c -5 kcal/mol indicates favorable binding.
Visualize docking poses with PyMOL (v2.5; Schrödinger, LLC).
All statistical tests were performed in R (v4.3.3).
A list of DEGs, CGs, and final biomarkers.
LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Boruta feature selections.
A nomogram with calibration, ROC, and DCA plots.
GSEA enrichment results and immune infiltration profiles.

steps.title: Download Transcriptomic Datasets
steps.instruction: Download the following datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gds/) on October 18, 2025:

substeps.instruction: Training set: GSE156035 (platform GPL20844), containing 20 T1D PBMC samples and 20 healthy control PBMC samples.
Validation set: GSE72377 (platform GPL10558), containing 15 T1D PBMC samples and 20 healthy control PBMC samples.

steps.title: Retrieve Phospholipid Metabolism-Related Genes
steps.instruction: Download a set of 212 phospholipid metabolism-related genes (PMRGs) from the Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB; https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb/) using the access date October 18, 2025.

steps.title: Perform Differential Expression Analysis
steps.instruction: Use the limma package in R to perform differential expression analysis on the training set (GSE156035 normalized expression matrix).

substeps.instruction: Apply thresholds: adjusted P < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| > 0.5.
Generate a list of differentially expressed genes (DEGs).

steps.title: Identify Candidate Genes
steps.instruction: Identify overlapping genes between the DEGs and PMRGs using the ggvenn package with the command: ggvenn(list(DEGs, PMRGs)) to obtain Candidate Genes (CGs).

steps.title: Perform GO and KEGG Enrichment
steps.instruction: Perform Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway enrichment on the CGs using clusterProfiler.

substeps.instruction: Set parameters: p-value cutoff = 0.05 and q-value cutoff = 0.2.
Visualize the top enriched terms.

steps.title: Construct PPI Network
steps.instruction: Construct a protein-protein interaction (PPI) network for the CG list.

substeps.instruction: Upload the CG list to the STRING database (https://string-db.org/) with a confidence score > 0.15.
Download interaction data and visualize using Cytoscape (v3.10.2).

steps.title: Perform Feature Selection
steps.instruction: Apply three machine learning algorithms to identify candidate biomarkers:

substeps.instruction: LASSO regression (glmnet): Use 5-fold cross-validation and select optimal λ (lambda.min).
SVM-RFE (e1071): Use 5-fold cross-validation and recursive feature elimination.
Boruta algorithm (Boruta package): Use 100 iterations and P < 0.01.

steps.title: Determine Final Candidate Biomarkers
steps.instruction: Use ggvenn to take the intersection of the LASSO, SVMRFE, and Boruta candidate biomarkers to obtain the final candidate biomarkers.

steps.title: Validate Biomarker Expression
steps.instruction: Validate the expression levels of the final candidate biomarkers in both the training and validation sets using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (P < 0.05).

steps.title: Perform ROC Curve Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis using pROC.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the area under the curve (AUC) for each biomarker.
Use a threshold of AUC > 0.7 to indicate good diagnostic performance.

steps.title: Select Final Biomarkers
steps.instruction: Select the final biomarkers based on consistent expression trends and high AUC in both cohorts.

steps.title: Build and Validate Nomogram
steps.instruction: Build a nomogram using the rms package based on the final biomarker expression in the training set.

substeps.instruction: Assess calibration using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test (P > 0.05) and a calibration curve.
Plot the ROC curve for the nomogram and calculate the AUC.
Perform decision curve analysis (DCA) using ggDCA to evaluate clinical utility.

steps.title: Analyze Biomarker Correlations
steps.instruction: Perform Spearman correlation between each final biomarker and all other genes in the training set using the base R cor() function.

steps.title: Run GSEA
steps.instruction: Run GSEA using clusterProfiler with the MSigDB KEGG gene set 'c2.cp.v2024.1.Hs.symbols.gmt'.

substeps.instruction: Set parameters: |normalized enrichment score (NES)| > 1 and adjusted P < 0.05.

steps.title: Analyze Immune Cell Infiltration
steps.instruction: Analyze immune cell infiltration using the training set normalized expression matrix.

substeps.instruction: Calculate enrichment scores for 28 immune cell types using single-sample GSEA (ssGSEA) implemented in GSVA.
Identify differentially infiltrated immune cells (DIICs) between T1D and control groups using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (P < 0.05).

steps.title: Perform Correlation Analysis with DIICs
steps.instruction: Perform Spearman correlation analysis using the psych package to analyze correlations between DIICs and between biomarkers and DIICs.

substeps.instruction: Apply thresholds: |correlation coefficient| > 0.3 and P < 0.05.

steps.title: Predict Targeting miRNAs
steps.instruction: Predict miRNAs targeting each final biomarker using the miRWalk (http://mirwalk.umm.uni-heidelberg.de/) and TarBase (https://dianalab.e-ce.uth.gr/tarbasev9/) databases.

steps.title: Predict Targeting Drugs
steps.instruction: Predict potential drugs targeting final biomarkers using DSigDB (Drug Signatures Database; https://dsigdb.tanlab.org/DSigDBv1.0/).

substeps.instruction: Select core drugs that target biomarkers with the highest combined scores.
Obtain protein structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB; https://www.rcsb.org/) or UniProt (https://www.uniprot.org/).
Obtain drug structures from PubChem (https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/).
